tradition.name: Tibetan pop
tradition.lineage: Dennis Rea — The Fellowship of Tsering, from Giant Steppes (2021). Representative authored present-day recording arrangement for the selected documented branch. Sources establish category, roles and locality. Exact materials, makes, playing settings, tuning, room, signal chain and axes are authored choices, not measured source-session facts or universal genre characteristics.

extras.description: Label explicitly describes mutant Tibetan pop and credits this Jampa Tsering reworking: Dennis Rea electric/organ guitars and kalimba; Greg Powers dungchen; Albert Kuvezin voice; Dick Valentine flute; Wadim Dicke electric bass; Steve Fisk keys, sounds/rhythms and processing; Daniel Zongrone drums/percussion; Avosound prayer-flag/wheel field recordings. Every positively named sound family remains represented. Explicit experimental reimagining of Tibetan popular songs, not a claim that Tibetan pop as a whole is experimental electronic music. One source-named live singer; field-recording contents are retained intact without inventing additional singer count. The guitar card preserves the credited electric-guitar family role; its stock clean-arpeggiated preset does not separately encode the source organ-guitar processing. No actual organ player or whole-ensemble effect is invented. This is an authored role-complete reproduction, not an exact timbral reconstruction. Sampler carries field-recording playback and Fisk sounds/rhythms/processing; separate workstation retains keys. Generic auxiliary percussion remains distinct from drum kit. These are authored processing and timbral abstractions, not original hardware claims. Dung chen construction and religious lineage remain unspecified.
